name: Vaser liposuction
lead: VASER (vibration amplification of sound energy at resonance) liposuction is a form of ultrasound-assisted liposuction in which a probe delivers ultrasonic energy to fat before it is suctioned out. It is described in the surgical literature as a third-generation ultrasound technique, introduced after earlier ultrasound devices that surgeons reported as bulky and associated with a higher potential for complications.[1][2]

In appearance culture it is best known as the tool behind high-definition liposculpture, sometimes called abdominal etching, in which fat is removed or shaped to emphasise the outline of muscle groups such as the abdominals. Surgeons who developed the approach reported using VASER to treat superficial fat layers and to define musculature as well as to reduce volume.[3][4]

The appearance chain is direct and local: ultrasonic energy loosens fat so it can be aspirated from chosen areas, removed fat cells do not come back in that spot, and with the fat layer thinned the outline of muscle shows, so a lean person with stubborn fat on the abdomen, flanks or chest can look more defined. Wikipedia states that the suctioned fat cells are permanently gone, while it also reports that overall body fat generally returns toward its prior level within months and redistributes, so it describes liposuction as body contouring rather than weight loss [5].

Published evidence consists mainly of surgeon-reported case series and a small number of comparative trials against conventional suction-assisted liposuction. Liposuction in general is described as removing fat locally without producing lasting weight loss.[5]

paras: VASER is a brand of ultrasound-assisted lipoplasty. Ultrasonic energy applied through a probe in the fat layer is intended to loosen fat so it can be aspirated, and authors of early reports compared it with earlier ultrasound-assisted devices as well as with conventional suction.[2] A general overview of liposuction notes that 1980s and 1990s ultrasound devices sometimes injured tissue through excess ultrasound exposure, while third-generation devices use pulsed energy and specialised probes.[5]
Surgeons describing the technique say it allows work on the superficial fat layer, which is the basis of high-definition approaches that aim to show muscle detail instead of only reducing bulk.[3]

Liposuction as a field began in the mid-1970s in Rome, where Arpad and Giorgio Fischer used a blunt cannula with suction on the outer thighs and called it liposculpture; Yves-Gerard Illouz extended it to the whole body and developed the wet technique, and Jeffrey Klein's tumescent method in the 1980s used large volumes of dilute anaesthetic so only local anaesthesia was needed [5]. Ultrasound-assisted devices of the 1980s and 1990s caused tissue injury through excess energy, and third-generation devices use pulsed energy and specialised probes [5]. A review series on ultrasound-assisted lipoplasty is available for current practice [14].

A modified Delphi panel of five US expert plastic surgeons produced 18 consensus statements for using VASER as an adjunct to liposuction, covering device settings, provider technique, postoperative instructions and management of side effects and complications. The authors noted that published guidelines had been lacking [13].

A 2007 report described VASER-assisted high-definition liposculpture as a way to improve contour and highlight underlying musculature, extending earlier differential lipoplasty techniques that had been limited to small areas in lean male patients.[3] Abdominal etching more broadly was first described in 1993.[5]
A 2018 report described 736 high-definition lipoabdominoplasties performed with circumferential VASER liposuction between 2005 and 2017, combining abdominal definition with abdominoplasty.[4]

A prospective study of 45 men with gynecomastia compared traditional liposuction, VASER, and VASER combined with J-plasma, reporting significant differences among groups in subareolar disc reduction, skin redundancy, the need for a second stage and satisfaction, with the combination described as effective for grade 2 and 3 gynecomastia [15]. A retrospective review of 180 patients examined Renuvion, a helium plasma skin-tightening device, including its frequency of use alongside VASER liposuction [16]. A single-centre study related BMI and aspirated fat volume to complications in VASER liposuction [17]. VASER has also been used within case series for lipedema and lymphedema [18][19].

High-definition liposculpture is discussed in looksmaxxing circles as a surgical route to visible abs or to removing stubborn fat that diet and training have not shifted. Proponents describe it as intended for people who have worked on diet and exercise but still have resistant areas, and as permanent removal of the treated fat cells. Fat removal from the chin or neck area is also one of the common uses of liposuction.

A 2002 pilot clinical study reported on VASER-assisted lipoplasty and compared its outcomes with those of other ultrasound-assisted devices.[2] A multicentre, prospective, randomised, single-blind trial published in 2012 used a contralateral design in 20 female patients to compare VASER-assisted and suction-assisted lipoplasty, and its authors noted that no earlier comparative study had shown a statistically significant benefit of a new technology over suction-assisted lipoplasty.[6] A registered trial of 21 participants compared the two approaches.[7]

Other published work includes a comparison of blood loss between suction-assisted and third-generation ultrasound-assisted lipoplasty,[8] a study of acute fat-cell viability after third-generation ultrasound liposuction,[9] and a review of complications of high-definition liposculpture and how they are managed.[10] A trial comparing adipose viability after liposuction is registered as recruiting,[11] and a registered study is evaluating rib osteotomy for waist narrowing as a separate body-contouring approach.[12]

The 2012 randomised trial used a contralateral design in 20 women aged 20 to 48, with each patient receiving VASER-assisted lipoplasty on one side and suction-assisted lipoplasty on the other [6]. The 2002 pilot study compared VASER with other ultrasound devices, which had been criticised for complications, bulky instrumentation, higher cost and a steep learning curve [2]. The 2007 report described applying VASER to superficial fat layers to highlight musculature, extending earlier differential lipoplasty that had been applicable only to limited areas in lean male patients [3]. The 2018 series spanned 736 high-definition lipoabdominoplasties between 2005 and 2017 [4].

Liposuction in general is described as considered safe but with risk that rises with the volume removed. Reported serious complications include deep vein thrombosis, organ perforation, bleeding, infection and fat embolism, and deaths have been estimated at about one per 10,000 cases as of 2011.[5] Early ultrasound devices were reported to carry additional potential for tissue injury and complications.[2] A dedicated review addresses complications specific to high-definition liposculpture.[10]

Wikipedia reports a 2015 study found complications in 1.5 percent of 4,534 patients treated by board-certified plastic surgeons, with risk rising when removed volume exceeded 100 ml per unit of BMI; swelling can persist for weeks or months, and seromas and altered sensation can occur [5]. A review of lipoplasty in the overweight patient describes large-volume liposuction by board-certified surgeons using energy-assisted devices as a procedure with minimal complications, when evidence-based protocols such as hypothermia prevention, DVT prophylaxis and antibiotic prophylaxis are followed [21].

timeline.event: Arpad and Giorgio Fischer develop suction liposculpture in Rome [5].
Pilot clinical study of VASER-assisted lipoplasty published.[2]
Randomised contralateral trial of VASER versus suction-assisted lipoplasty published.[6]
Report of 736 high-definition lipoabdominoplasties with VASER published.[4]
Five-surgeon Delphi panel publishes consensus recommendations for VASER ultrasound-assisted liposuction [13].

lore.intro: VASER and high-definition liposculpture are discussed on looksmaxxing forums as a surgical option for stubborn fat and abs definition.

claims.claim: Liposuction permanently removes fat cells in the treated area
claims.believers: Forum posters describe liposculpture as permanent mechanical removal of fat cells and recommend it for people with stubborn fat after diet and exercise.
claims.experts: Wikipedia says suctioned fat cells are permanently gone but overall body fat generally returns to earlier levels within months, partly in the abdomen, and that liposuction does not produce lasting weight loss. [5]

claims.claim: High-definition liposculpture can show abdominal muscle outlines
claims.believers: Surgeons and patients describe superficial-fat work as the way to show muscle detail rather than only reduce bulk. [3]
claims.experts: A 2007 report and a 736-patient series document the technique in surgeon-reported cases. [3][4]

claims.claim: VASER is a better liposuction than suction-assisted lipoplasty
claims.believers: Surgeons describe more precise, controlled results and less trauma. [17]
claims.experts: The 2012 contralateral randomised trial was designed to test this in 20 women, and its authors noted that no earlier comparative study had shown a statistically significant benefit of a new technology over suction-assisted lipoplasty. [6]

card.summary: Ultrasound-assisted liposuction used for body contouring and abs 'etching'; evidence is mostly surgeon case series plus a few small trials.
card.aka: VASER lipo, VASER Hi-Def, abdominal etching, high-definition liposculpture
card.note: Surgical procedure; liposuction carries risks including infection, bleeding and embolism.

quick.overview:
VASER is a brand of ultrasound-assisted liposuction. It uses ultrasonic energy to loosen fat before it is suctioned out and is widely associated with high-definition liposculpture, which aims to show muscle outlines such as the abdominals.

Published work is largely surgeon-reported case series, with a few small comparative trials against conventional suction liposuction.
quick.mechanism: A probe delivers ultrasonic energy into the fat layer, and the fat is then aspirated. Surgeons describe work on superficial fat as the basis of definition procedures.
quick.risks: Liposuction in general carries reported risks including infection, bleeding, blood clots, organ perforation and fat embolism, with risk rising with volume removed. A dedicated review covers complications of high-definition liposculpture.

chain: Probe delivers ultrasonic energy that loosens fat in chosen areas
Loosened fat is suctioned out, including from the superficial layer
Thinner fat over the muscle shows abdominal and torso definition
angle.text: VASER removes fat from selected areas, and surgeons using high-definition techniques sculpt the superficial fat so the outline of abdominal, chest or shoulder muscle is more visible. It reshapes the body without producing lasting weight loss.
